issues.description: The problem statement text (task description) specifies addGuestStudents(String) as the method signature, but the UML diagram, the template TODO reference, and the solution implementation use addGuestStudents(int). This inconsistency can lead students to implement the wrong parameter type and fail tests or be confused about the expected signature.
issues.suggestedFix: Correct the problem statement to specify addGuestStudents(int) as the required method signature (matching the UML, template guidance, and solution). Alternatively, if the intention was to accept a String, update the UML, template, and solution to use String consistently — but preferrably change the textual description to int to match the rest of the materials.

issues.description: The problem statement's prose indicates the method signature addGuestStudents(String), while the UML in the same problem statement and the reference solution implement addGuestStudents(int). This mismatch of the parameter type for the same conceptual operation (adding a number of guest students) can confuse students about the expected method signature and data type to use.
issues.suggestedFix: Unify the specification: change the prose in problem_statement.md from addGuestStudents(String) to addGuestStudents(int) and explicitly state that the method accepts an integer number of new guest students. Ensure the UML and any textual descriptions consistently show addGuestStudents(int) to match the template/solution implementation. Alternatively, if a String was intended, update the solution and template to accept a String and document the expected format—prefer using int for numeric counts.
